pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: packages/producers/src/publish/timers.ts:20 The publish context's two loops are named once from a closed set, and each TimerSpec registers its cadence, deadline and staggered first firing. The tick body reports when the next slot is due, sweeps orphans and downtime misses through the steady-state code path, and stops at safe points between claims. A store-read status surface also exposes staleness, standing failure and quarantine, so this context supplies what the background-jobs envelope needs.

techniques.evidence: packages/producers/src/publish/timers.ts:20 Closed name roster. TimerSpec carries name, everyMs, deadlineMs and firstDelayMs, so cadence and first-tick delay sit in the registration, not the body. Each timer is a kernel lease on timer:<name> with a TTL of three missed beats (timerTtlS, line 44): a heartbeat claim with slack.

packages/producers/src/publish/timers.ts:27 Each loop declares a per-tick deadline in its spec (30 min for publish-tick). Abandoned work is fenced, so it cannot corrupt shared state. Inside the body, publishClaimed catches adapter throws per slot (publish.ts:117) and records them as slot failures, so one bad slot costs one outcome, not the tick. Crash capture, the re-entrancy skip and quarantine run in the worker envelope (workers/timers.ts), which is outside this context.

packages/producers/src/publish/tick.ts:51 The tick returns the earliest still-scheduled slot (computed at tick.ts:89), so the loop can wake at that slot's time. The 30 s idle cadence stays as the safety net, and timers.ts:33 states the worst-case latency next to the constant. firstDelayMs staggers boot (0 vs 60 s), a deliberate stagger rather than random jitter. The metrics cadence is justified next to its constant by quota.

packages/producers/src/publish/timers.ts:75 A read-only current-state surface: one row per roster entry with lastRunAt, nextDueAt, stale (silence via lease heartbeat lapse or a dead process), the standing failure verbatim, and quarantined. Transitions only (timer.fail/recover/quarantine/gap), not one event per tick. Two partial gaps: there is no explicit consecutive-failure count (failing.since stands in) and no last-success time separate from the heartbeat.

packages/producers/src/publish/tick.ts:74 The startup catch-up is the steady-state sweep itself, the publish-tick's first firing at firstDelayMs 0. It reports missed, interrupted (claims held by dead holders), drifted and cleared slots. A miss inside the downtime gap is attributed with downtime {from, to} in the same commit as the miss.

packages/producers/src/publish/tick.ts:82 Cooperative stop at safe points between claimed uploads. Unstarted claims fail with a stated cause (STOPPED_TEXT, publish.ts:53), never left phantom-running. Uploads heartbeat the claim per chunk (the keeper in publish.ts), which serves as the is-it-moving signal. A lost fence stops the sender. Outcomes are a closed published/failed/lost set keyed by slot id. An upload already in flight is an uncancellable span; there is no done/total progress, only liveness.

packages/producers/src/publish/tick.ts:106 Nothing here is a budgeted wait on a tracked operation that can give up and wait again. publish-now runs the tick inline and awaits its result. The only deadline (deadlineMs) abandons and fences the work, which is the cancellation contract this technique excludes.
